newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia disowns Iraq envoy's no-fly zone rejection.
newsitem.headline: Russia disowns Iraq envoy's no-fly zone rejection.

text.p: The Russian Foreign Ministry sought to distance itself on Monday from remarks by one of its diplomats in Baghdad that Moscow did not recognise allied no-fly zones and defended Iraq's right to shoot at warplanes enforcing them.

Itar-Tass news agency quoted a senior official in Moscow as saying: "The authenticity of this statement is being checked...But in any case I can say that such statements do not correspond in any way to Russia's position."

Vladimir Titorenko, deputy head of the Russian mission, had told Reuters on Sunday: "We do not recognise either of the no-fly zones, in the north and south. This country has the right to protect itself. When they have warplanes of another country flying over their airspace they have the right to shoot."
The official said Russia had asked Iraq to drop a threat to fire on U.S. and other allied planes enforcing the zones. Baghdad backed away from the threat on Friday.

Titorenko also told Reuters that Moscow saw the dispatch of more U.S. troops to the region as an attempt by Washington to escalate tension and said President Bill Clinton was massing troops to win November's presidential election.

Earlier on Monday, Russia's deputy foreign minister Viktor Posuvalyuk told Interfax news agency that a planned visit to Moscow on Tuesday by his Iraqi opposite number, Riyad al-Qaysi, was not anti-American.
Russia intended to share news of the talks with Washington and other interested parties, said Posuvalyuk, who was on a mission to Baghdad shortly before the first U.S. missile strikes against Iraq.
